title: Coco
director: Lee Unkrich; co-directed by Adrian Molina
cast: Anthony Gonzalez, Gael García Bernal, Benjamin Bratt & Ana Ofelia Murguía (voices)
setting: Fictional Santa Cecilia, Mexico, and a fantasy Land of the Dead
basis: Original story drawing on Día de Muertos traditions
overview: Miguel’s pursuit of music uncovers a family story that has been misremembered. Examine how songs, objects, and testimony connect identity with remembrance.
essential: How does discovering a fuller family story change Miguel’s choices?
goals: Explain how family memory shapes character choices.
Support an interpretation with two accurately described scenes.
Compare the portrayal with an appropriate external source and identify what remains uncertain.
prep: Introduce remembrance, family narrative, evidence, and musical motif. Explain that Miguel is the young protagonist and Coco is his great-grandmother. Discuss the film’s fantasy separately from varied real Día de Muertos practices; no required family-loss disclosures.
context: Use a teacher-selected cultural source to contextualize the tradition without treating one fictional family as representative of all Mexican people. The same song has different meanings depending on its performer, audience, and relationship.
pauses: Pause after the music ban is explained, after meeting Héctor, after the family revelation, and before the final song with Coco.
warnings: Skeleton imagery, death, a murder revelation, and threats of being forgotten.
Grief, separation, and distress involving an elderly family member.
Peril and some intense confrontations despite the colorful fantasy setting.
discussion: How does discovering a fuller family story change Miguel’s choices?
Which scene best supports your interpretation, and what might another viewer notice?
What does the film leave out or simplify?

online.section: Before viewing
online.question: How can a family story change when new evidence appears?
online.answer: An omitted perspective or detail can alter the meaning of an inherited account.

online.section: Before viewing
online.question: Why can the same song mean different things to different listeners?
online.answer: Relationships and circumstances affect how its words and performance are understood.

online.section: Part A · Music and family rules
online.question: Why does Miguel’s family reject music?
online.answer: An inherited account of abandonment connects music with harm to the family.

online.section: Part A · Music and family rules
online.question: Why does Miguel admire Ernesto de la Cruz?
online.answer: Public fame and performances offer a model for the musical future he wants.

online.section: Part A · Music and family rules
online.question: How does the damaged family photograph influence his assumption?
online.answer: An incomplete image leads him to connect the missing ancestor with the famous musician.

online.section: Part A · Music and family rules
online.question: What changes after he takes the guitar?
online.answer: The fantasy places him in the Land of the Dead, creating a new problem and search.

online.section: Part A · Music and family rules
online.question: Why does Imelda’s condition on her blessing matter?
online.answer: Miguel must negotiate between returning home and continuing music.

online.section: Part B · Searching for the story
online.question: How does Héctor’s need differ from Miguel’s goal?
online.answer: Héctor wants to reach the living world before remembrance of him disappears.

online.section: Part B · Searching for the story
online.question: What does the forgotten musician’s disappearance reveal?
online.answer: The fantasy gives memory a concrete role in sustaining the dead.

online.section: Part B · Searching for the story
online.question: How do Miguel and Héctor help one another initially?
online.answer: They exchange skills and access while pursuing different immediate needs.

online.section: Part B · Searching for the story
online.question: Why does Ernesto’s public image become unreliable evidence?
online.answer: Celebrity performance conceals harmful actions and appropriation of another person’s work.

online.section: Part B · Searching for the story
online.question: What does Miguel learn about Héctor’s family connection?
online.answer: Héctor is Coco’s father, changing the meaning of the family’s story.

online.section: Part C · Truth and remembrance
online.question: How does the murder revelation alter the apparent abandonment?
online.answer: It shows that a forced separation was mistaken for a voluntary rejection.

online.section: Part C · Truth and remembrance
online.question: Why does returning become urgent?
online.answer: Héctor’s survival in the fantasy depends on Coco’s remaining memory.

online.section: Part C · Truth and remembrance
online.question: Why does Miguel sing to Coco rather than merely present an argument?
online.answer: The personal song offers a connection to her remembered relationship with her father.

online.section: Part C · Truth and remembrance
online.question: What changes in the family’s later remembrance?
online.answer: Héctor’s place and music are restored within a fuller account of the past.

online.section: After viewing
online.question: Which object functions as evidence, and what are its limits?
online.answer: Analyze the photograph, guitar, or letters without assuming an object explains everything alone.

online.section: After viewing
online.question: How does one song’s changing use develop the theme?
online.answer: Compare two performances and explain how context changes meaning.

online.section: After viewing
online.question: What cultural question should be checked beyond the fantasy?
online.answer: Select a question about Día de Muertos and use a reliable cultural source.

online.section: After viewing
online.question: How does the ending connect artistic ambition with responsibility?
online.answer: Miguel can pursue music while recognizing family relationships and the need for truthful remembrance.
